title: Simon Commission and the Nehru Report

faqs.q: The Government of India Act, 1919 provided for a commission to review the working of the governance scheme after how many years?
Who was the chairman of the Indian Statutory Commission?
On what date was the Simon Commission set up?
faqs.e: It was constituted under the prime ministership of Stanley Baldwin.

faqs.q: Who was the British Prime Minister when the Simon Commission was set up?
Which Secretary of State for India was responsible for the appointment of the Simon Commission?

Consider the following pairs:
(I) Lee Commission – Recruitment of British officers in the Raj
(II) Mudiman Commission – Deadlock within the diarchic dispensation
(III) Linlithgow Commission – Crisis of Indian agriculture
Which of the pairs given above is/are correctly matched?
What was the most distinctive feature of the composition of the Simon Commission that provoked Indian opposition?

options.a: It was chaired by an Indian
options.b: It was an all-white, seven-member commission
options.c: It had a Congress boycott built in

faqs.a: It was an all-white, seven-member commission

faqs.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the reasons for the early appointment of the Simon Commission:
(I) The Conservative government feared losing power to the Labour Party and did not want constitutional reforms decided under a Labour government.
(II) Several parliamentary inquiries by the mid-1920s had already pointed to the failure of the 1919 Act.
(III) Universal adult franchise had already been guaranteed in most European countries by this time.
Which of the above is/are correct?
Under whose presidency did the Congress session at Madras (December 1927) decide to boycott the Simon Commission?
At the Madras session of December 1927, Jawaharlal Nehru got a snap resolution passed declaring what as the Congress goal?

Consider the following statements about the Muslim League's response to the Simon Commission in 1927:
(I) At its Calcutta session under Jinnah, the League decided to oppose the Commission.
(II) At its Lahore session under Muhammad Shafi, the League supported the government.
Which of the above is/are correct?
Which of the following groups decided NOT to boycott the Simon Commission?

options.c: Jinnah's faction of the Muslim League

faqs.e: The Unionists in Punjab also chose not to boycott.

faqs.q: On which date did the Simon Commission land in Bombay, triggering a countrywide hartal?
Which body appointed Dr Ambedkar to work with the Simon Commission?
In which month did Dr Ambedkar go before the Simon Commission?
On behalf of which organisation did Ambedkar submit a memorandum to the Simon Commission on rights and safeguards for the depressed classes?

Consider the following statements regarding Ambedkar's submissions to the Simon Commission:
(I) He argued for universal adult franchise for both men and women alike.
(II) He stated that the depressed classes had no link with the Hindu community and should be regarded as a distinct, independent minority.
(III) He demanded representation for the depressed classes on the same basis as the Mohammedan minority.
Which of the above is/are correct?
What did Ambedkar propose if universal adult franchise was NOT granted?

options.a: A separate electorate for the depressed classes

faqs.a: A separate electorate for the depressed classes
faqs.e: If universal franchise WAS granted, he instead sought reserved seats for the depressed classes.

faqs.q: What condition did the Simon Commission's report attach to the reserved seats it granted the depressed classes?

options.b: Candidates had to be nominated by the Viceroy
options.c: Candidates' competence had to be endorsed by the provincial governor

faqs.a: Candidates' competence had to be endorsed by the provincial governor
faqs.e: Ambedkar was displeased with this condition, and in any case the provision remained a dead letter.

faqs.q: What was a significant social feature of the countrywide protests against the Simon Commission?

options.a: It was led entirely by princely states
options.b: A new generation of youth got their first taste of political action

faqs.a: A new generation of youth got their first taste of political action

faqs.q:
Consider the following statements about radical youth groups linked to the anti-Simon Commission upsurge:
(I) Punjab Naujawan Bharat Sabha
(II) Workers' and Peasants' Parties
(III) Hindustani Sewa Dal, based in Karnataka
Which of the above emerged in this context?
Which two Congress leaders emerged as leaders of the new wave of youth and student protest against the Simon Commission?

options.b: Lala Lajpat Rai and G.B. Pant
options.c: Tej Bahadur Sapru and Ali Imam

faqs.q: In which city were Jawaharlal Nehru and G.B. Pant beaten up by police during anti-Simon Commission protests?
On what date did Lala Lajpat Rai die from the injuries of a police lathicharge?
faqs.e: He received the fatal blows during a lathicharge in October 1928.

faqs.q: Which of the following was NOT among the two-fold impacts of the Simon Commission's appointment on the national movement, as described?

options.a: Lord Birkenhead's challenge for an agreed constitution was accepted, raising hopes for Indian unity
options.b: It gave stimulus to radical forces demanding socio-economic reforms on socialist lines
options.c: It gave Congress an issue to forge mass action around
options.d: It led to the immediate grant of dominion status

faqs.a: It led to the immediate grant of dominion status

faqs.q: Whose challenge to Indian politicians to produce an agreed constitution was accepted by various political sections following the Simon Commission's appointment?
In which month and year did the Simon Commission publish its two-volume report?
What did the Simon Commission's report propose regarding dyarchy in the provinces?

options.a: Its abolition, with representative government and autonomy for provinces

faqs.a: Its abolition, with representative government and autonomy for provinces

faqs.q: According to the Simon Commission's report, in relation to what matters was the governor to have discretionary power?

options.b: Internal security and administrative powers to protect different communities

faqs.a: Internal security and administrative powers to protect different communities

faqs.q:
Consider the following statements about the Simon Commission's recommendations for the centre:
(I) It rejected parliamentary responsibility at the centre.
(II) The governor-general was to have complete power to appoint cabinet members.
(III) The Government of India would have complete control over the high court.
Which of the above is/are correct?
On the question of electorates, what did the Simon Commission's report recommend?

options.d: Retention (and extension) of separate communal electorates until Hindu-Muslim tensions subsided

faqs.a: Retention (and extension) of separate communal electorates until Hindu-Muslim tensions subsided

faqs.q: What federal-level body did the Simon Commission's report suggest be established, to include representatives of British provinces and princely states?

Consider the following statements on territorial changes recommended by the Simon Commission's report:
(I) Sindh should be separated from Bombay.
(II) Burma should be separated from India.
(III) NWFP and Baluchistan should get local legislatures and representation at the centre.
Which of the above is/are correct?
faqs.e: Burma's separation was justified on the ground that it was not a natural part of the Indian subcontinent.

faqs.q: What did the Simon Commission's report recommend regarding the Indian army?

options.a: Indianisation of the army while retaining British forces
options.c: Complete withdrawal of British forces immediately

faqs.a: Indianisation of the army while retaining British forces

faqs.q: Why had the Simon Commission's report lost much of its relevance by the time it was published?

options.a: Several events had overtaken the importance of its recommendations by then
options.b: Sir John Simon resigned before publication
options.c: It was rejected by the British Parliament

faqs.a: Several events had overtaken the importance of its recommendations by then

faqs.q: The Nehru Report was drafted by a sub-committee appointed by which body, in response to Lord Birkenhead's challenge?
In which month and year did the All Parties Conference appoint the sub-committee to draft a constitution?
Who chaired the committee that drafted the Nehru Report?

Consider the following statements about the Nehru Committee:
(I) Its members included Tej Bahadur Sapru, Subhash Bose, and Shuab Qureshi.
(II) It was the first major Indian attempt to draft a constitutional framework for the country.
(III) Its report was finalised by August 1928.
Which of the above is/are correct?
On what basis of government did the Nehru Committee's recommendations divide, with the majority favouring one position and a section (including Nehru) favouring another?
faqs.e: The majority favoured dominion status; the minority section (prominently including Nehru) wanted complete independence, with the majority granting this section liberty of action.

faqs.q: What geographical scope did the Nehru Report confine itself to?

options.a: All of the Indian subcontinent including Burma
options.b: British India only, envisaging future federal link-up with princely states
options.c: British India and princely states equally

faqs.a: British India only, envisaging future federal link-up with princely states

faqs.q: What form of government did the Nehru Report recommend for the dominion?

options.b: Dominion status on the lines of self-governing dominions

faqs.a: Dominion status on the lines of self-governing dominions

faqs.q: On electorates, what did the Nehru Report recommend?

options.b: Rejection of separate electorates, in favour of joint electorates with reserved Muslim seats where they were a minority
options.c: Reserved seats for Muslims even in provinces where they were a majority
options.d: Retention of separate electorates for all communities

faqs.a: Rejection of separate electorates, in favour of joint electorates with reserved Muslim seats where they were a minority
faqs.e: Provinces where Muslims were already in a majority, such as Punjab and Bengal, were excluded from this reservation.

faqs.q: How many fundamental rights did the Nehru Report recommend, including equal rights for women and the right to form unions?

Consider the following statements about the central legislature proposed in the Nehru Report:
(I) The House of Representatives was to have 500 members elected on adult suffrage, with a 5-year tenure.
(II) The Senate was to have 200 members elected by provincial councils, with a 7-year tenure.
(III) The governor-general was to be appointed by the British government but paid out of Indian revenues.
Which of the above is/are correct?
What tenure did the Nehru Report propose for provincial councils?
Besides responsible government and fundamental rights, which of the following did the Nehru Report also recommend?

options.a: A unitary state with no provincial autonomy

faqs.q: What did the Nehru Report recommend regarding the relationship between the State and religion?

options.a: Complete dissociation of the State from religion
options.b: Continuation of the existing communal electoral system
options.c: State patronage for the majority religion

faqs.a: Complete dissociation of the State from religion
faqs.e: The report also promised full protection to the cultural and religious interests of Muslims.

faqs.q: Who acted on the advice of the provincial executive council under the Nehru Report's proposed provincial structure?
The 'Delhi Proposals' emerged from a Muslim League session held in which month and year?
Which Congress session accepted the Muslim League's Delhi Proposals?

Consider the following statements regarding the Delhi Proposals:
(I) They called for joint electorates in place of separate electorates, with reserved seats for Muslims.
(II) They demanded one-third representation for Muslims in the Central Legislative Assembly.
(III) They demanded the formation of three new Muslim-majority provinces — Sindh, Baluchistan, and NWFP.
Which of the above is/are correct?
What structural demand did the Hindu Mahasabha make regarding the constitution, alongside opposing new Muslim-majority provinces?

options.a: A federal structure with strong provinces

faqs.q:
Consider the following statements about the concessions made in the Nehru Report to Hindu communal opinion:
(I) Joint electorates were proposed everywhere, but reservation only where Muslims were a minority.
(II) Sindh's separation from Bombay was to occur only after dominion status was granted, and subject to weightage for the Hindu minority in Sindh.
(III) The political structure proposed was broadly federal, with residual powers resting with the provinces.
Which of the above is/are correct?
faqs.e: Statement III is incorrect — the Nehru Report's structure was broadly unitary, with residual powers resting with the centre, not the provinces.

faqs.q: What dilemma did Motilal Nehru and the other drafters of the Nehru Report face during deliberations?

options.b: Choosing between dominion status and independence
options.c: Deciding the tenure of the Senate
options.d: Balancing Muslim League demands against the risk of losing Hindu communalist support, and vice versa

faqs.a: Balancing Muslim League demands against the risk of losing Hindu communalist support, and vice versa

faqs.q: At which city's All Parties Conference session (December 1928) did Jinnah propose amendments to the Nehru Report?

Consider the following statements about Jinnah's amendments to the Nehru Report:
(I) One-third representation for Muslims in the central legislature.
(II) Reservation for Muslims in Bengal and Punjab proportionate to population, till adult suffrage was established.
(III) Residual powers to the provinces.
Which of the above is/are correct?
faqs.e: These amendments were not accommodated by the All Parties Conference.

faqs.q: In which month and year did Jinnah put forward his Fourteen Points?
Jinnah's Fourteen Points became the basis for the future propaganda of which faction of the Muslim League?
Which of the following was one of Jinnah's Fourteen Points?

Consider the following statements about Jinnah's Fourteen Points:
(I) They demanded a federal constitution with residual powers to provinces.
(II) They demanded one-third Muslim representation in the central legislature and in any cabinet.
(III) They demanded that territorial redistribution not affect the Muslim majority in Punjab, Bengal, and NWFP.
Which of the above is/are correct?
Angered by the Nehru Report's dominion status proposal, which two leaders jointly set up the Independence for India League?

options.a: Tej Bahadur Sapru and Ali Imam

faqs.e: The younger Congress section regarded dominion status as a step backward and rejected Congress's modified goal.
